$comment: The error taxonomy every SDK maps. Mirrors dsp-backend app/errors/codes.py, which is a closed StrEnum. `concept` is the language-neutral name used by conformance cases; each SDK maps it to an idiomatic class. `retry` is normative: an SDK that retries a code marked false is a bug.
type_uri_rule: docs_base + code with '.' and '_' replaced by '-'
notes: Branch on `code`. Never on `title` or `detail` — those are prose and may be reworded.
Error bodies are rendered with exclude_none, so any field except type/title/status/code may be absent.
An unrecognised code must fall back to the class for the HTTP status, never raise.
402 and 429 are never conflated. 402 is commercial and carries no Retry-After; waiting does not help.
Every response, success or error, carries the request_id in the X-Request-Id header.

codes.meaning: Every pre-authentication failure, collapsed into one answer: no credential, an unusable session, a cookie that did not travel. Deliberately indistinguishable so an anonymous caller cannot map the auth model. The real reason is logged against request_id.
No X-API-Key header was sent.
The key is malformed, unknown or revoked. Revocation takes effect immediately.
The key passed its expiry. Keys last 365 days by default, 730 at most; there is no non-expiring key.
The key is valid but lacks the scope this endpoint requires.
The request carried both an Origin header and an API key. Keys are server-side only; there is no CORS allowlist. Rejected in middleware before routing.
The identity service could not be reached. Transient.
Dashboard sign-in only. One code for both a wrong password and a nonexistent account — separating them is an account-existence oracle.
Dashboard sign-up only.
A dashboard-session route was called with an API key. Not reachable from an SDK.
Dashboard only. Not reachable from an SDK.
Dashboard only. Not reachable from an SDK.
Validation failed. Field-level detail is under extra.errors. Note the server forbids unknown body fields and its message does not name them — the SDK should reject unknown parameters locally first.
The request body exceeded the size cap.

Unsupported content type (415). Also the 422 a relationships question gets when the corpus cannot answer it: `extra.kind` says which refusal (`no_anchor`, `wrong_route`, …) and `extra.try_instead`, when present, suggests a rewording.
A relationship anchor resolved to more than one company or institution. Name it more precisely — a domain or LinkedIn URL rather than a name, or `kind` on an institution.
No history entry with that id for this tenant. A 404 rather than a 403 even when the row belongs to someone else: confirming it exists would leak that it does.
The search or run a report names does not exist, or is not this caller's. One code for both on purpose: distinguishing them would say whether another tenant's search exists.
The feedback store is unreachable. Bounded retry is reasonable; the report was not saved.
The store that records dashboard journey events is unreachable. Dashboard-only: no API-key route returns it.
The internal company-enrichment lookup is not configured or unreachable. Internal-only: no API-key route returns it.
No such saved list in this workspace. Missing, deleted and another workspace's list are deliberately the same answer.

Adding these items would take a free workspace past its saved-items cap. Nothing was added. `extra` carries `cap`, `saved` and `adding`, so you can tell how many still fit. An entity already saved in another list does not count again.
The saved-lists store is unreachable. Nothing was changed.
CSV export is switched off in this deployment. Retrying will not help; the route answers once export is enabled.
The sign-up cohort question is not offered right now. Dashboard-only: no API-key route returns it.
An admin impersonating a user cannot answer the cohort question for them. Dashboard-only.
This account has already used its one referral code. Dashboard-only.
An admin impersonating a user cannot claim a referral code for them. Dashboard-only.

The cursor is malformed, failed signature verification, or does not match this request. The last case is the common one: a cursor is signed against a fingerprint of the request that produced it, so every field except `limit` must be resent unchanged.
The cursor is older than 24 hours. Re-run the search; do not retry with the same cursor.
Paging beyond 10,000 results. Narrow the search instead.
A request with this Idempotency-Key is still running.
This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request body.
Too many calls to one operation from this workspace in the current minute. `extra` carries `limit`, `window` and `operation`. Honour Retry-After, which is never more than a minute.
Daily request quota exhausted. Retry-After may be hours away.
Monthly request quota exhausted.
Too many requests in flight for this key.
Too many distinct entities retrieved in a rolling window. An anti-enumeration limit.
The admin console's rate-limit settings store is unreachable. Internal-only: the limiter itself falls back to its default policy, so no `/v1` route returns it.
Not enough credits for this action. Carries no Retry-After, deliberately: waiting does not help, buying does. Never retried, never slept on, never conflated with a 429.
The credit service could not be reached. Transient; Retry-After: 5.
No pricing row for this action. A server misconfiguration, not a client error — and never a free pass. It does not self-heal, so it must not be retried.
Not a purchasable amount. Raised only by the dashboard's billing routes, which a key cannot reach; mapped by meaning so `.code` still names the cause.
The caller may not buy credits for this tenant. Dashboard billing routes only.
The payment provider is unreachable. Dashboard billing routes only; bounded retry is reasonable.
The card was refused. Also a 402, but deliberately not `credits.insufficient`: one means the card said no, the other that the balance is empty. Dashboard billing routes only.
No card on file — a missing prerequisite rather than a failed purchase. Dashboard billing routes only.

A top-up handle that is unknown, expired, or another workspace's — one answer for all three, so a handle cannot be used to probe other tenants. Raised by the key-authenticated top-up routes, which the SDKs do not wrap; mapped so `.code` still names the cause.
Retrieval was unreachable. Nothing was charged: a billed call is charged only once its answer is ready.
Retrieval exceeded its budget. The work is abandoned and not billed.
The server is the limitation, not the request. Distinct from request.invalid, which means you asked for something invalid. Retrying will not help.
An unhandled server error. Bounded retry is reasonable.

status_fallbacks.$comment: Used when a response carries a code this SDK version does not know. Never raise on an unknown code.
